1: A 74-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, ischemic stroke, peripheral arterial disease, bilateral nonobstructive renal artery stenosis, chronic right internal carotid occlusion, seizures, and vascular dementia was transferred from a nursing home because of decreased oral intake and dehydration for at least one week.
2: Initial laboratory results were notable for acute renal failure and severe metabolic acidosis: sodium 145 mEq/L, potassium 6.6 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 207 mg/dL, creatinine 10.2 mg/dL (baseline 1.1 mg/dL), glucose 185 mg/dL, chloride 106 mEq/L, bicarbonate 8 mEq/L, anion gap 31, venous pH 7.09, and lactate 4.4 mmol/L.
